### Observed differences

- In the later window, A10 is executed far less often: it appears in about 7–8 in 100 traces versus about 35 in 100 before (15 vs 70 of 200 traces), and its mean occurrences per trace fell from about 0.36 to about 0.08. [OCC001]
- A10's surroundings thinned accordingly: its outgoing transitions, previously about 85% leading to A19 or A20, now spread thinly over roughly a dozen activities (none above about 20%); A45 rarely leads to A10 anymore (about 30 in 100 of A45's outgoing transitions before, about 2 in 100 after); and A10 co-occurs with the main activities A25, A26, A27, A30, A35, A36, A41, A42 and A45 in about 7–8 in 100 traces versus about 35 in 100 before. The lag profiles involving A10 now rest on only 1–5 after-window observations. [DIR001, DIR008, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG010]
- The four activities A35, A36, A41 and A42 swapped sides relative to A26 and A27: before, they ran before A26 and A27 in about 99 in 100 traces; in the later window they run after them in about 98–99 in 100, while all six activities still occur together in every trace in both windows. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017]
- Routing at the boundaries of that four-activity block flipped: A25's next activity changed from one of the four (about 24–26% each) to A27 in about 99 in 100 cases; A26's next activity changed from A30 (about 99 in 100) to one of the four (about 18–30% each); and each of the four now leads to A30 (about 21–27%) where it previously led to A27 (about 23–25%). [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- Adjacency confirms the swap: A25 is now immediately followed by A27 (about 99 in 100) where A27 previously came five positions later; A30 now follows A26 about five positions later where it previously immediately followed; A36 followed by A27 within five steps essentially disappeared (200 traces before, 1 after) and A35 followed by A30 appeared (1 before, 199 after). [LAG006, LAG007, LAG009, LAG008]
- Event positions moved consistently with the swap: A27 and A26 occur earlier (mean relative position about 0.48 to 0.37 and 0.62 to 0.52), while A35, A36, A41 and A42 occur later (about 0.41 to 0.58), each based on all 200 traces in both windows. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural rearrangement in which the block of four activities A35, A36, A41 and A42, which previously ran between A25 and A27, now runs between A26 and A30: A25 leads directly to A27, A26 leads into the block, and the block exits to A30. The order reversal is shown directly — co-occurrence stays at 100 in 100 traces while the before/after order flips almost completely — and it is matched by the successor changes at A25, A26 and the four block activities, by the boundary lags flipping between immediate and five positions apart, and by the consistent position shifts. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]

A second, distinct difference is A10's near-disappearance: executed in about 35 in 100 traces before and about 7–8 in 100 after, consistent with that part of the process being skipped or run far less often; the evidence does not show whether this belongs to the same rearrangement or is an independent change, and the after-window lag profiles for A10 rest on only 1–5 observations. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR008, REL001, REL009, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]

The two distinct differences clearly exceed the roughly 0.83 qualifying items expected by chance across the 166 tested units, and every item's difference is larger than in about 199 of 200 random re-splits; an important competing explanation that remains is a shift in the mix of process variants — for example, two coexisting variants with different block placements sampled in different proportions — which finite 200-trace windows cannot fully rule out, although near-complete flips on full support in both windows make pure sampling variation implausible. [OCC001, DIR002, DIR003, REL010, LAG006, LAG007]
